{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The Thursday, when it arrived, was ordinary in the way he had suspected it would be. Rain in the morning, then not. He opened at nine because he always opened at nine, and the bell above the door sounded the same as it had on the Wednesday.

He took the envelopes out from under the paperweight and put them on the counter, squared them, and then put them back. Then took them out again. There were four. He had not opened the fourth. He knew its handwriting and he knew, roughly, what it would say, and he had found over the winter that knowing roughly was a place a person could live for quite a long time.

A boy came in wanting a book about ships for a school project and he sold him one that was too old and too good, and did not charge him for it, and the boy left looking suspicious. That was fair. He would have been suspicious too.

At noon he walked to the corner to look at the lifted tar. It had lifted further. A bus had caught it and dragged a strip loose, and it lay curled on the kerb like something shed. He stood over it a while. Then he went back and rang the council, and gave the road name, and his own, and said yes when they asked if he would be there if someone came round.

He opened the fourth envelope at twenty past two. Ines's handwriting. Two lines. He read them and set the letter down and moved the Portuguese verse to the shelf by the window, where it caught the light, and left it there."}
